- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 10-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from 10-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.17) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast based on recent 5-day momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% upward bias for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.22), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and use 14-day smoothed price as anchor.
- If true outcome exceeds model by > 3% for 3 consecutive days, apply mean reversion rule: next forecast = prior forecast + 0.5×(true - forecast) for next 3 days.
